testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Formally ask you to fix your vehicle's problems.
Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a vehicle unsafe, they can take it out of service until the problems are fixed.

questions.question: When testing a parking brake, the vehicle should:

options.text: Be in low gear while the driver tries to pull forward.
Be inspected by a professional mechanic.
Be driven while the parking brake is on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be in low gear while the driver tries to pull forward.
questions.explanation: To test a parking brake, fasten your seat belt, set the parking brake, release the trailer parking brake if needed, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it needs to be fixed.

questions.question: When starting the engine during the pre-trip inspection, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: When checking your engine during the pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
Do not work well on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS activates during hard braking to prevent wheels from locking up.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a busy area near trees.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in an open area.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop immediately. Park in an open area away from anything that could catch fire, like trees or other vehicles. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: Sending text messages while driving:

options.text: Is okay if the messages are short.
Is allowed if you are asking your employer a question.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is not allowed.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, a driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Turn back after the vehicle is straight again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, remove your foot from the brake to let the locked wheels roll again. Turn quickly in the direction you want to go, then turn back to prevent skidding in the opposite direction.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger side than the driver side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fully raised.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a trailer, make sure the landing gear has no missing parts and is fully raised. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: When inspecting a power steering system, you should check that:

options.text: The fluid is at the right level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses have no fluid in them.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the right level.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for and repair any leaks before driving.

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum is created when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction inside a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: How much water does a road need for a vehicle to hydroplane?
questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. This can happen with just a small amount of water.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds how many feet to your stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to total stopping distance.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not made to drive in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Fresh rain mixes with oil and grease on the road and creates a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump brakes three times, then push the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump brakes three times, then push the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump brakes three times, then push the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump brakes three times, then push the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump brakes three times, then push the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times and hold it firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak.

questions.question: How do you warn drivers behind you when you need to brake?

options.text: Tap the brakes a couple of times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a couple of times.
questions.explanation: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, lightly tap the brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safety of loaded cargo?

options.text: Only the driver can load cargo.
Someone else can load cargo, and they are responsible for its safety.
Someone else can load cargo, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
Only a professional loader can load cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Someone else can load cargo, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
questions.explanation: Even if someone else loads the cargo, the driver must inspect it, make sure it is properly secured, and make sure it does not block the view or access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: Why should you not stare at one mirror for too long?

options.text: Looking at mirrors can make you drowsy.
You can drive a long distance without looking at the road.
The mirror may not show an accurate view.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive a long distance without looking at the road.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often but quickly. Staring at one mirror too long means you are not watching what is ahead of you.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes in air brake systems must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: For vehicles with air brakes, how should the air compressor drive belt be checked?
questions.correctAnswerText: It should be tight.
questions.explanation: Before each drive, check the air compressor drive belt. It should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, how can a driver slow down?

options.text: Let the truck run out of gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear helps slow your vehicle when hydraulic brakes fail.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do with your mirrors?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Use them only when there is traffic.
Check them regularly, but only on cloudy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of your surroundings at all times.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice. Drive extra carefully on melting ice.

questions.question: What is the maximum leakage rate for air brakes on a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: The leakage rate must not exceed 3 psi in one minute. Higher leakage means the system needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: What can happen if cargo is improperly loaded?

options.text: It looks bad to other drivers.
It can injure the driver during a quick stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can injure the driver during a quick stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly loaded and secured. During a quick stop, unsecured cargo can fall and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: How does night driving compare to daytime driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: It is more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. Poor visibility, headlight glare, and more fatigued or impaired drivers make nighttime driving riskier.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: Do not leave space on your right while turning right. Other drivers may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: After stopping during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not activate the four-way flashers because it is just a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Activate the four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Activate your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Speed up as you approach the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Always keep both hands on the steering wheel when turning quickly to avoid a hazard. A firm grip allows you to turn quickly and safely.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, what should the driver do?

options.text: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed legal weight limits.
Unseal the load to check safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed legal weight limits.
questions.explanation: Drivers cannot open sealed loads, but they must verify the load does not exceed gross weight and axle weight limits.

questions.question: Which braking system uses the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: The service brake system
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when the driver presses the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black from dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may look wet but is actually icy.

questions.question: What should you do with a burning tire?

options.text: Cut it up with an axe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cool it with water.
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use large amounts of water to fully cool the tire.

questions.question: How can a driver check if the road is becoming icy?

options.text: Open the window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icing up, open your window and touch the front of your side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on these items, the road is likely icing up too.

questions.question: When entering traffic, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for your vehicle to accelerate slowly, especially if it is loaded.
Make sure you can cross traffic without getting in the way.
Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic, remember how large your vehicle is and how much space it needs to accelerate. Wait for a big enough gap before accelerating. Your vehicle needs more space if it is heavily loaded. Always make sure you can completely cross traffic without interfering with other vehicles.

questions.question: How can you best reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone to receive calls.
Use the phone to text instead of talk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid all cell phone distractions, turn off your phone before you start driving and keep it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
You can turn to face the road before you finish exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face toward the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before turning, what should you do?

options.text: Stop past the stop line for a better view.
Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly before the stop line, crosswalk, or sign. Keep your front wheels pointed straight and do not let the vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see its rear tires.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you get points for:

options.text: Exiting the vehicle one time to check your positioning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing over an exercise boundary.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each time this happens, you lose points on your skills test score.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle running while adding coolant.
Not use gloves to touch the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant to a system without a recovery tank. Wear gloves or use a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release the pressure.

questions.question: Extremely hot temperatures can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tire failure.
questions.explanation: When temperatures rise, air inside tires expands and tire pressure increases. This can cause tire failure. Check your tire pressure regularly when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a backing maneuver in the basic control skills test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blind offset
questions.explanation: Backing maneuvers in the basic vehicle control skills test include straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: By tapping the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, a knob controls the parking brake. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push the knob in to release them.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined weight of a vehicle plus all the cargo it is carrying.

questions.question: What is the penalty for driving a hazmat CMV while under the influence of alcohol?

options.text: Losing your CDL for three months
Losing your CDL for six months
Losing your CDL for one year
Losing your CDL for three years

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing your CDL for three years
questions.explanation: Driving a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) under the influence of alcohol usually results in losing your CDL for at least one year. If you are driving a hazmat CMV while under the influence of alcohol, you lose your CDL for at least three years.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, you should set it to:

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the control to normal.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Research has shown this valve does not help. Always leave it in the "normal" position for full stopping power.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Obtain special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to get them to move from the lane closest to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obtain special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy require special permits. Drivers of these loads must follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank.
Are used to drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are used to drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in brake systems collect water and compressor oil that must be drained. If you do not drain them, your system can be damaged. Use the manual drains at the end of each driving day.
